## How to Interpret This File

- This voluntary context file is not access control, a formal indexing directive, a ranking signal, or a guarantee that any system will use or cite it.
- Crawler allowance only expresses a public crawl preference. It does not prove a crawl, indexing, ranking, model inclusion, answer inclusion, or citation.
- The XML sitemap is the indexable-route inventory. Aliases and noindex pages are intentionally omitted; noindex is not a privacy or authorization boundary.
- Structured data identifies public entities and relationships. It does not independently prove biographical, product, client, performance, or outcome claims.

## Current Summary

Sulayman Bowles is a UT Austin student working in AI product at Chegg, building Atlas technical SEO software, running Void Agency, and publishing research on AI systems, crawlability, infrastructure, and investment questions.

Atlas is a crawl and evidence console. Void Agency is the fixed-scope technical SEO practice. The technical ledger is a separate record of experiments and technical work. Sulayman is pursuing a BA in Music alongside the BBA in Finance.

## Canonical Entities and Source Roles

- [Canonical Person entity](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/about#sulayman-bowles): Stable graph identifier anchored on the About page; the fragment is an entity ID, not a separate document.
- [Primary identity source](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/about): Current public profile and mainEntityOfPage for the Person entity.
- [Official site root](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/): Canonical WebSite and publisher context.
- [Code evidence](https://github.com/SulaymanB2024): Controlled public code profile; repository existence does not prove every product claim.
- [Professional profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sulayman-bowles/): Controlled corroborating profile; time-sensitive facts should be checked against visible dates.
- [Technical work record](https://sulayman-bowles.tech/): Separate technical ledger, not a duplicate canonical identity site.
- Use visible dates and linked public support for material claims.
- Do not infer private client names, rankings, traffic, revenue impact, or provider coverage from missing public data.
- Atlas is a crawl and evidence system; Void Agency is a fixed-scope technical SEO practice.

## Indexability Contract

- [Canonical host](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/): The apex host is authoritative for this site.
- The www host redirects to the apex canonical host.
- [XML sitemap](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/sitemap.xml): Only canonical HTML routes in this inventory are intended for indexing.
- Alias, retired, prototype, and archive-methodology routes are omitted from the XML sitemap; generated noindex metadata is the route-level exclusion signal.
- Canonical links, Open Graph URLs, WebPage URLs, Article URLs, and sitemap locations are required to converge on the same canonical URL.
- [Resume redirect destination](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/resume): The retired 2025 PDF resume alias redirects here.
- Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, and IndexNow submissions are discovery and recrawl signals; they do not prove rankings, indexing, traffic movement, or AI citations.

## Crawler Policy

- [robots.txt](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/robots.txt): Host-scoped crawl preference; advisory rather than access control.
- [Crawler policy source map](https://sulayman-bowles.dev/research/ai-search-crawler-policy-sources.csv): Published row-level verification dates remain in the file; this policy contract was reviewed 2026-07-30.
- Conventional search crawlers: Googlebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot are explicitly allowed.
- AI answer-search crawlers: OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot are explicitly allowed for public discovery.
- User-triggered retrieval agents: ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User are explicitly allowed, but provider documentation determines whether robots.txt applies to a user-initiated fetch.
- Model-development crawlers: GPTBot, ClaudeBot are explicitly allowed as a deliberate public-crawl preference, independent of answer-search crawlers.
- User-Agent text alone does not authenticate a crawler. Server-log attribution should also use current provider-published IP ranges where available.
